questions.question:
In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option.If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.

We have to always be on our (1)/guard to ensure the highest level (2)/of safety inside train operations. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** '1'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the given sentence, the error lies in the placement of the adverb "always."
 
• The correct rule states that **adverbs of frequency, such as "always,"** should be placed directly after the first auxiliary verb if there is more than one verb in the sentence.
 
• In this case, **"have" i**s the auxiliary verb that precedes the base verb** "be."**
 
• Therefore, the correct phrasing should be "We always have to be on our guard." 
 
• Thus the correct option is 1 and therefore the answer.

questions.question:
In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.

He also identified quality of catering, (1)/ linen and cleanliness, which (2)/ he said was crying in attention. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution: The error lies in part 3. The correct preposition that will be used in place of 'in' will be 'for. Thus, teh correct answer would be 'crying for attention'.

questions.question:
In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.

Mr. Batra took a card from ______ pocket.
questions.solution: The correct pronoun here is ‘his’ as it is used for belonging to or associated with a male person or animal previously mentioned or easily identified. Thus option 3 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it

by selecting the appropriate option.

The rich ______ not always happy.
questions.solution: The correct verb is ‘are’ as the word ‘rich’ here signifies the rich people. Thus a plural verb is needed here. Option 2 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the one which best expresses the meaning of the given word.

Defy
questions.solution:
The meanings of the words are:

Defy=>openly resist or refuse to obey.

Give in=> agree

Obey=> submit to the authority of (someone) or comply with (a law)

Repel=> drive or force (an attack or attacker) back or away

Surrender=> give in

Thus option 3 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the one which best expresses the meaning of the given word.

Laden
questions.solution: The word ‘laden’ means ‘full or filled with.’ The word ‘unloaded’ means ‘unpacked.’ Thus option 1 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the one which best expresses the meaning of the given word.

Lousy
questions.solution: The word ‘lousy’ means ‘very bad.’ Thus option 2 is the correct answer. The word ‘magnificent’ means ‘splendid.’

questions.question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the one which is opposite in meaning of the given word.

Eternity
questions.solution:
The word ‘eternity’ means ‘infinite or unending time.’ The meanings of the other words are:

Perennial=> lasting or existing for a long or apparently infinite time

Bounds=> limits

Mortality=> the state of being subject to death

Thus option 4 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the one which is opposite in meaning of the given word.

Manage
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Fail**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **"Manage":** refers to achieving something or handling situations effectively. (प्रबंध करना)

 
 
• Example: You can manage this situation.
 
 
 
• The opposite in meaning to "Manage" is "Fail".

questions.question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the one which is opposite in meaning of the given word.

Resolve
questions.solution: The word ‘resolve’ means ‘determination.’ Thus ‘indecision’ is the correct antonym as it means ‘the inability to make a decision quickly.’ The word ‘intend’ means ‘aims’ and ‘firmness’ means ‘the quality of having a solid, almost unyielding surface or structure.’ Thus option 2 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
In the following question, out of the four given alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

Set at liberty
questions.solution: The idiom ‘set at liberty’ means ‘to release.’ Thus option 1 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
In the following question, out of the four given alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

Get away
questions.solution: The idiom ‘get away’ means ‘escape.’ Thus option 2 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Improve the bracketed part of the sentence.

Schools (which) have gyms do not have enough facilities such as swimming pools and tennis courts.
questions.solution: The word ‘which’ is the correct determiner here and needs no change. Thus option 4 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Improve the bracketed part of the sentence.

Workers work for over twenty five hours per week to get (them) minimum wages.
questions.solution: The correct pronoun here is ‘their’ as it means ‘belonging to or associated with the people or things previously mentioned or easily identified.’ Thus option 1 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
In the following question, out of the four given alternatives, select the alternative which is the best substitute of the phrase.

A brief account of a subject
questions.solution:
The meanings of the words are:

Arbitrary=> based on random choice or personal whim, rather than any reason or system

Temporary=> not permanent

Summary=> A brief account of a subject

Adversary=> opponent

Thus option 3 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
In the following question, out of the four given alternatives, select the alternative which is the best substitute of the phrase.

A body of voters
questions.solution:
The meanings of the words are:

Administrate=> less common term for administer

Corporate=> relating to a large company or group

Electorate=> all the people in a country or area who are entitled to vote in an election

Confederate=> joined by an agreement or treaty

Thus option 3 is the correct answer.

questions.question: In the following question, a word has been written in four different ways out of which only one is correctly spelt. Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.solution: The correct word is ‘clever’ which means ‘wise.’ Thus option 2 is the correct answer.

questions.question: In the following question, a word has been written in four different ways out of which only one is correctly spelt. Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.solution: The correct word is ‘guarantee’ which means ‘provide a formal assurance, especially that certain conditions will be fulfilled relating to a product, service, or transaction.’

questions.question:
Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.

A mere visit

P: computer depending on

Q: the programs used

R: to a website can infect
questions.solution: R is the first statement as it states where the visit is made. P follows R as it states what is affected. Q states on what it depends. Thus option 4 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.

We have no safer water

P: inhale and pollution

Q: to drink pure air to

R: free land to crop
questions.solution: Q must be the first statement as ‘drink’ is mentioned here. P follows Q as ‘inhale’ fits after the word ‘air.’ R completes the statement. Thus option 1 is the correct answer.

questions.question: Rural development was ______ with the launching
questions.solution: The word ‘initiated’ means ‘started’ and fits here. The word ‘depreciated’ means ‘diminished’ and does not fit here. The other words too do not convey any meaning.

questions.question: Very ______ but it had promoted
questions.solution: The presence of ‘although’ and ‘not’ help us to understand that the word here must convey a positive meaning. Thus option 2 is the correct answer. The word ‘ineffective’ means ‘unsuccessful’ and ‘ruthless’ means ‘merciless.’ Both the words do not convey any meaning here.

questions.question: The ______ of a network of basic extension
questions.solution: Programmes are held for a positive intention so the correct word here is ‘growth’ which conveys the meaning that the network was to be expanded. The word ‘dispute’ means ‘a disagreement.’ The word ‘eruption’ means ‘rash or outbreak.’

questions.question: Services at the grass ______ level in villages.
questions.solution: The only word that fits here is ‘root’ as the phrase ‘grass root’ means ‘the most basic level.’ Thus option 4 is the correct answer. The word ‘mere’ means ‘only’ and does not fit here.

questions.question: Technological ______ in agriculture possible later in the mid 60's.
questions.solution: The correct word is ‘advances’ as it conveys a positive meaning. The sentence talks about awareness so it must convey something positive. The word ‘conflict’ means ‘dispute’ and ‘inflict’ means ‘cause (something unpleasant or painful) to be suffered by someone or something.’ The word ‘solicits’ means ‘ask for or try to obtain (something) from someone’. These words do not convey a proper meaning here.
